_meta.indication: ELUCIREM is a gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated in adult and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older for use with MRI to detect and visualize lesions with abnormal vascularity in the central nervous system (brain, spine, and associated tissues) and the body (head and neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis, and musculoskeletal system).

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, crossover phase 3 study; each patient received MRI with gadopiclenol and with gadobutrol comparator.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with known or highly suspected lesions of the central nervous system (brain and spine).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Three co-primary lesion visualization endpoints (border delineation, internal morphology, and degree of contrast enhancement) for paired pre- and post-contrast gadopiclenol MRI versus pre-contrast MRI alone.
pivotal_trials.n: 256 patients randomized; 247 received gadopiclenol; primary efficacy analysis in FAS 1 (239 patients).
pivotal_trials.result: All three co-primary visualization endpoints met predefined success criteria: 95% CIs above 0 at their lower bound for all three readers and p<0.0001 for all differences (paired vs pre-contrast).

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, crossover phase 3 study; design identical to GDX-44-010 for non-CNS body regions.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with known or highly suspected enhancing lesions in the head and neck, thorax (including breast), abdomen, pelvis, or musculoskeletal system.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Three co-primary lesion visualization criteria (border delineation, internal morphology, degree of contrast enhancement) for paired gadopiclenol MRI plus noncontrast MRI versus noncontrast MRI.
pivotal_trials.n: 304 patients randomized; 288 received gadopiclenol; primary efficacy analysis in FAS 1 (278 patients).
pivotal_trials.result: All three co-primary visualization endpoints met predefined success criteria: 95% CIs above 0 at their lower bound for all three meta-readers and p<0.0001 for all differences.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >0.2%) at 0.05 mmol/kg (n=708): injection site pain (0.7%), headache (0.7%), nausea (0.4%), injection site warmth (0.4%), injection site coldness (0.3%), dizziness (0.3%), and localized swelling (0.3%). Class risks include hypersensitivity, nephrogenic systemic fibrosis, and gadolinium retention.
target_moa: Gadopiclenol is a nonionic, macrocyclic gadolinium complex that alters the relaxation rates of hydrogen nuclei in water, changing signal intensity on T1-weighted MRI in a concentration-dependent manner; it has higher relaxivity than currently marketed GBCAs, allowing use at a lower dose.
modality: Small molecule (macrocyclic gadolinium-based contrast agent / metal chelate).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: NEPHROGENIC SYSTEMIC FIBROSIS (NSF) — NSF has occurred in patients with impaired elimination of GBCAs; higher than recommended dosing or repeat dosing appear to increase the risk.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting or other external consultation was needed for this NDA.

description.text: Extended existing indications to pediatric patients under 2 years of age, including term neonates

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application updates the U.S. Prescribing Information to include an extension of the existing Elucirem indications to pediatric patients < 2 years of age, including term neonates. In addition, this supplement provides for revisions to subsection 8.1 Pregnancy to reflect clinical experience regarding the risk of in utero exposure to gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) based on a review of scientific literature.

basis.text: Priority review was granted on the basis of unmet medical need, as there are no U.S. approved and marketed MRI contrast agents indicated for musculoskeletal lesion visualization.

citations.quote: The Applicant requested a priority review, which was granted on the basis of unmet medical need as there are currently no U.S. approved and marketed MRI contrast agents indicated for musculoskeletal lesion visualization.

summary.text: This was a standard (traditional) 505(b)(1) NDA approved under priority review granted on the basis of unmet medical need; no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, or orphan designation applied, and no advisory committee was convened.

requirement.text: 4341-1: Deferred pediatric study — conduct a study of approximately 40 neonates and infants aged <2 years receiving a single 0.05 mmol/kg dose of gadopiclenol IV for evaluation of plasma pharmacokinetics (POP-PK); safety and imaging data as secondary endpoints.

citations.quote: 4341-1 Conduct a study of approximately 40 neonates and infants aged < 2 years that will receive a single dose of 0.05 mmol/kg gadopiclenol intravenously for the evaluation of the plasma pharmacokinetics profile of gadopiclenol (POP-PK analysis). Safety and imaging data will be collected as secondary endpoints.

requirement.text: 4341-2: Conduct a developmental and perinatal/postnatal reproduction study of gadopiclenol by IV bolus in mice, including postnatal behavioral/functional evaluation (GDX-33-073), examining safety and gadolinium retention in brain and other organs.

citations.quote: 4341-2 Conduct a developmental and perinatal/postnatal reproduction study of gadopiclenol by intravenous (bolus) injection in mice, including a postnatal behavioral/functional evaluation (Sponsor Reference No. GDX-33-073).

requirement.text: 4341-3: Conduct an IV (bolus) juvenile toxicity study of gadopiclenol in mice (GDX-33-072), examining safety after repeated administration and gadolinium retention in brain and other organs/tissues.

citations.quote: 4341-3 Conduct an intravenous (bolus) injection juvenile toxicity study of gadopiclenol in mice (Sponsor Reference No. GDX-33-072).
